home.title: The TypeScript framework where you write business code first, choose deployment and API later.
home.subtitle: Declare your domain once. Validation, tables, API and forms derive from it, and one config line decides where each part runs.
home.slogan: The TypeScript framework where you write {code} first, choose deployment and API {later}.
home.plateCredit: R. Siélain, Atlas de poche des plantes des champs, pl. 124, 1895
home.codeText: Plain classes that do the work and ask for what they need. No route, no setup, no server required.
home.schemaText: You describe a post once, and your code uses it everywhere.
home.derivationText: The API, the validation, the form and the table are all read from your schema. Change a field and they change with it.
home.derivationCalls: Incoming — REST, GraphQL, forms, client types
home.derivationCaption: One field added to an entity: the table, the form and the API follow.
home.choicesText: One process or several, which implementation answers each port, SQLite or Postgres: each is one line in fougere.config.ts, completed by your editor from your own code. Your code doesn't change.
home.choicesCaption: One line in fougere.config.ts: the blog answers from its own process, and the page keeps working.
home.ruleText: Tables, protocols, hosts: Fougere keeps them apart from what your code means, so changing them never touches it.
home.derivationDoc: Get forms and an API from your schema
